behavioralGoal: Clients and representatives can request support, check upcoming visits or follow a pending request without scanning competing full-size dashboard cards.
knownAudience: Existing client portal users and representatives; desktop and mobile. Individual accessibility needs and task times are unknown.

flows.sequence: Book support > service > preferred date > review services, notes, categorized room videos and consent > office confirmation
flows.hesitation: Which action is primary; is the booking confirmed?
flows.feedback: Selected service/date and review form; existing saved-request confirmation retained
flows.recovery: Change service, go back, close review without submission

flows.sequence: Repeat previous service or choose Upcoming/Requests
flows.hesitation: Panels used to appear or disappear depending on window height
flows.feedback: Pressed view button, record counts, single matching task panel
flows.recovery: Switch back without submitting a request

flows.sequence: No bookings or requests > clear empty state > Book support; no date > review disabled; no worker profiles > ask office
flows.feedback: Explanatory text and office confirmation wording
flows.recovery: Primary navigation and help remain available

ledger.participantsTask: Meta-analysis: 50 published/unpublished experiments, 63 conditions, 5036 participants; varied choice tasks
ledger.finding: Near-zero mean effect with substantial between-study variation
ledger.boundary: A synthesis of older heterogeneous choice tasks; does not establish the optimum number of care services or prove this design is faster
ledger.decision: Keep all six services with named groups. Remove duplicate presentation and clarify task views instead of deleting choices.
ledger.falsifier: Clients cannot find the right service or require more backtracking in task testing

ledger.participantsTask: Accessibility standard for pointer inputs, including users with motor limitations; not a participant study
ledger.finding: 24 CSS px minimum with specified exceptions; larger important controls can be beneficial
ledger.boundary: Normative minimum does not guarantee successful interaction
ledger.decision: Use 44px primary/view/worker controls and visible keyboard focus
ledger.falsifier: Rendered targets overlap, are undersized, or keyboard users cannot reach them

ledger.participantsTask: Accessibility guidance for enlarged and narrow-viewport content, especially low vision; not an experiment
ledger.finding: Content should retain information/functionality without two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px, subject to exceptions
ledger.boundary: Viewport checks are not a full WCAG audit or a test with assistive-technology users
ledger.decision: Natural content height, no height-dependent task navigation, one-column narrow layout, relative body sizes
ledger.falsifier: 320px or enlarged text loses a control, clips content, or requires horizontal scrolling

ledger.source: Local inspection plus ui-design-index > ui-design-systems; informed by the cited constraints
ledger.finding: Competing height rules stretched empty panels and shrank worker controls; short-window CSS changed which views appeared
ledger.boundary: The proposed hierarchy is a design hypothesis, not established product research
ledger.decision: Single task panel, readable worker sidebar, calendar preview on demand and full calendar in the date step
ledger.falsifier: Clients miss an upcoming visit or cannot locate the calendar after the change

patterns: Readable secondary controls and explicit empty states
architecture: Client home page, model, calendar, calendar preview and worker panel in frontend/features/client-home; layout, booking and worker CSS separate; reusable portal primitives in frontend/shared/portal.
unresolved: No client usability study or screen-reader audit
suggestedUsabilityCheck: Ask a client to find the next visit, request cleaning with a kitchen video, and locate a pending request. Record completion, misclicks and backtracking.
